program_name: The full official English name used on unibz's own documents is 'International Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity' — this is the exact header of both the 2026/27 admission-information PDF and the 2026/27 brochure, and the hero heading of the programme page ('International Master in' on one line, 'Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity' on the next). The short form used in navigation, in the signed ranking list ('Admission to the Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity') and in the PDF filenames is 'Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity'. The programme is commonly abbreviated FSIA by the partner universities (the University of Parma files it under the URL slug 'cdlm-fsia'). The Italian ministerial/AlmaLaurea registration carries a bilingual title: 'Scienze degli alimenti per l'innovazione e l'autenticità - food sciences for innovation and authenticity (LM-70)'. unibz does NOT translate the name: the Italian and Ladin navigation both read 'Master in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity'. Delivered by the unibz Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences. LANGUAGE-VERSION NOTE, unusual for unibz: there is NO German version of the programme page at all (https://www.unibz.it/de/... returns HTTP 404), and the Italian and Ladin URLs return only a stub carrying the notice 'Siamo spiacenti, questa pagina non è disponibile in italiano. Vai alla pagina in inglese.' The English page itself displays 'This page is only available in English'. unibz's ranking-list index files the programme under the heading 'Late Application for Inter-university Masters', alongside Environmental Management of Mountain Areas, Energy Engineering and Industrial Mechanical Engineering.
level: Master (Italian 'laurea magistrale', second-cycle degree, EQF/NQF level 7). 120 ECTS over 2 years / 4 semesters, degree class LM-70. Entry qualification is a bachelor degree; at enrolment the Diploma Supplement must show 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. JOINT DEGREE, NOT A SINGLE-UNIVERSITY AWARD — this is the single most important structural fact about the programme and it is stated far more explicitly by the partner universities than by unibz. The University of Udine's official course page states verbatim: 'Il corso di laurea magistrale inter-ateneo, internazionale in Food Sciences for Innovation and Authenticity è istituito tra la Libera Università di Bolzano (sede amministrativa), e le Università degli Studi di Udine e Parma con rilascio del titolo congiunto.' ('The inter-university, international master's degree course ... is established between the Free University of Bolzano (administrative seat) and the Universities of Udine and Parma, with the award of a JOINT DEGREE.') The 2021/22 University of Parma brochure says the same from the Parma side: the course 'is offered by tree [sic] joint Italian institutions (Free University of Bozen/Bolzano - administrative head, University of Parma and University of Udine) in cooperation with the University College Cork, Cork, Ireland and the Technical University of Munich, Munich, Germany.' PROFESSIONAL QUALIFICATION — REAL AND VERIFIED: LM-70 is the Italian degree class that gives access to the state examination for the profession of Food Technologist. unibz's own Italian-language faculty page confirms it hosts that examination: 'Dal 2020 la Libera Università di Bolzano è sede degli esami di Stato per l'abilitazione all'esercizio della professione di Tecnologo alimentare.' ('Since 2020 the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano has been a seat of the state examinations for qualification to practise the profession of Food Technologist.') The 2021 Parma brochure states the requirement plainly: 'A professional practice exam called "esame di stato" in Italy must be passed to enroll in the Food Technologists professional register.' Graduates also gain access to doctoral study; unibz runs a directly related PhD in Food Engineering and Biotechnology in the same faculty. [uncertain] Whether a non-Italian graduate can sit the Tecnologo Alimentare state examination without additional steps, and how the joint diploma is physically issued (one parchment signed by three rectors versus three separate parchments), is not documented on any of the three universities' public pages and should be confirmed with the Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it).
teaching_language: FULLY ENGLISH-TAUGHT, START TO FINISH, WITH NO SECOND OR THIRD LANGUAGE ANYWHERE IN THE PROGRAMME. This is NOT one of unibz's trilingual programmes. Brochure 'At a Glance', verbatim: 'Courses will be taught in English'. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English.' The only admission language requirement is English B2; there is NO German and NO Italian requirement at entry, NO third-language B1 threshold gating exams, and NO exit/graduation language requirement. VERIFIED AT COURSE LEVEL, NOT JUST IN THE MARKETING TEXT: the unibz 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' page for 2026/27 lists every single teaching unit with an explicit language tag, and every one of them — the whole first year, all four second-year profiles, the three 'Mobility activity' units and all twelve free-choice courses — is tagged 'EN'. Not one course in the published catalogue is offered in German or Italian. This is a stronger guarantee than most unibz English-taught masters can show, and it holds even for the courses taught by University of Udine and University of Parma staff (e.g. Sabrina Moret, Sonia Calligaris and Lara Manzocco from Udine; Daniele Del Rio, Pedro Mena and Alessia Levante from Parma), which appear in the unibz catalogue in English. THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT IS TRILINGUAL BUT THE DEGREE IS NOT: Bolzano is officially bilingual German/Italian, and one of the programme's own published alumni testimonials notes taking optional German classes ('After a first year in Bolzano, where I took the opportunity to attend German language classes thanks to the University's trilinguism proactive setup'). Language Centre courses in German and Italian are available on a voluntary basis and are worth taking for the South Tyrolean food-industry job market, but they carry no admission or graduation consequence. [uncertain] For students who choose the Udine, Parma or University College Cork second-year profile, the admission documents do not state whether any locally-offered elective at the host institution might be delivered in Italian; the unibz catalogue tags all listed units EN, but the host universities' own wider elective menus are not reproduced there. Confirm with the degree course director before choosing a partner profile.
campus: PRIMARY CAMPUS: Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. The brochure 'At a Glance' box states simply 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano' — unlike the sister inter-university master EMMA, this programme does NOT advertise a second campus in its headline data, even though its second year can be taken abroad. TWO PHYSICAL SITES IN BOLZANO. (1) The main campus, Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano (Advisory Service, tel. +39 0471 012100), with the Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences Secretariat at Universitätsplatz 5 / piazza Università 5 (tel. +39 0471 017000, agriculture@unibz.it). (2) NOI TECHPARK, the South Tyrolean science-and-technology park on the southern edge of Bolzano, which houses this programme's teaching laboratories. Brochure, verbatim: 'The teaching laboratories of this master offer hands-on training in food production, analysis, and quality assessment. Located at NOI Techpark, they feature facilities for food processing, sensory evaluation, and chemical, physical, and microbiological analysis.' Students on this master therefore commute between the city-centre campus and NOI Techpark; unibz's own emergency-contact page treats 'Bolzano centro e NOI Techpark Bolzano' as two distinct locations with separate laboratory emergency numbers. This is a laboratory-heavy programme — the published 'Hands-on Experience' items include cheese-making, green-tea antioxidant extraction, iron/plant nutrition work, DNA extraction and natural-leavening bread work. SECOND YEAR: THE CAMPUS DEPENDS ON THE PROFILE CHOSEN. Year 1 (61 CP) is taken at unibz by everyone. From year 2 the profile determines the host institution: 'Innovation and Authenticity of Wines' stays at unibz in Bolzano; 'Food Quality Control and Management' is offered at the University of Udine (Friuli Venezia Giulia, ca. 300 km east of Bolzano); 'Nutrition Sciences' at the University of Parma (Emilia-Romagna, ca. 250 km south); 'Food Chemistry' at University College Cork, Ireland (School of Food & Nutritional Sciences). The programme page adds: 'Students will have the opportunity to spend up to two semesters in one of these European partner institutions.' The thesis (33 CP) may be carried out at unibz, at a partner university, at a foreign university or jointly, and is frequently co-supervised with a food company. NOT a Brixen-Bressanone or Bruneck-Brunico programme, and — unlike EMMA — NOT a fixed two-country programme: the Bolzano-only route through the Wines profile is fully available. [uncertain] It is genuinely unclear how much physical relocation the Udine and Parma profiles involve. The published 2026/27 unibz course catalogue lists the Udine profile courses (Advanced sample preparation techniques and analysis of food contaminants; Management systems of food safety and quality; Food structure and physical properties) and the Parma profile courses (Human Nutrition; Applied human nutrition; Industrial microbiology for food quality improvement) INSIDE the unibz course offering, taught by Udine and Parma professors, which may mean they are delivered in Bolzano by visiting staff rather than requiring the student to move. The University of Parma's page, by contrast, describes the profile-specific teaching as taking place at the partner universities in the third semester. This directly affects housing, cost of living and (for non-EU students) residence-permit planning, and must be confirmed with the Faculty before choosing a profile.
degree_class: LM-70 — 'Scienze e tecnologie alimentari' (Food Sciences and Technologies), the Italian ministerial second-cycle degree class for the food industry. CONFIRMED BY FOUR INDEPENDENT SOURCES, so the 'to be verified' flag in the research brief can be closed: (1) the unibz brochure 'At a Glance' box, verbatim 'Degree class: LM-70'; (2) the unibz programme page's own At a Glance block, 'Degree class: LM-70'; (3) the University of Udine course record, 'LM-70 Scienze e tecnologie alimentari'; (4) the AlmaLaurea/ministerial registration, 'Scienze degli alimenti per l'innovazione e l'autenticità - food sciences for innovation and authenticity (LM-70)', class 'Scienze e tecnologie alimentari (LM-70)', also rendered by AlmaLaurea in English as 'LM 70 - Food Industry'. The signed 2026/27 ranking list confirms it functionally by using LM-70 in its double-enrolment illustration: 'the two programmes must not belong to the same class, e.g., LM-70/LM-70'. TWO TEMPLATE ERRORS IN UNIBZ'S OWN DOCUMENTS — worth knowing so they are not mistaken for real information. (a) The 2026/27 admission-information PDF's double-enrolment paragraph reads 'they do not belong to the same class (e.g. LM-73 and LM-73)' — LM-73 is the class of the sister programme EMMA, and the sentence is plainly copy-pasted from the EMMA template. (b) The signed ranking list repeats the double-enrolment rule twice, and its SECOND occurrence, in the 'Confirmation of study place and enrolment' section, reads 'e.g., LM-18/LM-18' — LM-18 is the Computer Science class used in the Software Engineering template. Neither error changes the programme's actual class, which is LM-70 in every substantive source. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES: (1) double-enrolment rule — a student may enrol in at most two programmes simultaneously, which must not share a class and 'must differ in at least two-thirds of their content'; (2) LM-70 is the class that opens the Italian state examination for Tecnologo Alimentare (Food Technologist), for which unibz has been an examination seat since 2020; (3) LM-70 is the natural second cycle above the Italian bachelor class L-26 (Food Sciences), which is why L-26 heads the list of directly-qualifying bachelor classes.
admission_type:
RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato / 'programmazione locale' in the University of Udine's registration), decided by a purely DOCUMENT-BASED, ARITHMETIC ranking. There is NO entrance exam, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT, NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video presentation and NO INTERVIEW. Together with EMMA this is one of the two simplest admission procedures at unibz.

MECHANICS, verbatim from the admission-information PDF and the signed ranking list (identical wording): 'If the number of eligible applicants exceeds the maximum number of available places (see section "Available places"), you will be assessed for admission based on your academic qualifications. The Admission Committee can assign up to a max. of 95 points based on the: final bachelor grade expressed out of 30 (for applicants already graduated); weighted grade average expressed out of 30 (for applicants not graduated yet). The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude). Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points. Minimum score for admission is 55/95 points.'

SO THE PROCEDURE HAS EXACTLY FOUR STAGES: (1) an ELIGIBILITY CHECK on the entry qualification — one of four Italian bachelor classes, or 30 ECTS across a very wide list of scientific sectors; (2) a LANGUAGE GATE at English B2, failure of which means exclusion from the procedure regardless of grade (8 EU applicants were excluded on this ground in Early Bird 2026/27); (3) an ARITHMETIC SCORE out of 95 derived from the bachelor grade, plus 2 for cum laude and plus 3 for a C1 English certificate; (4) a stated MINIMUM of 55/95.

A MANDATORY STRUCTURED EXCEL FILE must be uploaded: 'Excel file: Please use the file available in the application portal.' Applications go through the unibz Application Portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup.

TIE-BREAK, in order: 'If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet. In the event of further equal score, the younger applicant will be given priority (art. 3 L. 127/1997).' This mattered in 2026/27: EU ranks 13 and 14 both scored 83.77, and non-EU waiting-list ranks 16 and 17 both scored 78.76.

ADMISSION COMMITTEE for 2026/27, from the signed ranking list: President Prof. Matteo Mario Scampicchio (who is also the Degree Course Director); Members Prof. Youry Pii and Dr. Ksenia Morozova. Appeals may be lodged with the Bozen-Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days of publication.

HISTORICAL NOTE: the 2021/22 Parma brochure described access as 'Open access (Up to 35 EU students + 5 non-EU students)', i.e. capped but not competitive in practice. AlmaLaurea's records for 2024/25 and 2025/26 describe the committee as awarding 'up to 100 points'; the current unibz documents say 95. The scale appears to have been changed, and AlmaLaurea's figure should be treated as stale.
academic_requirements:
TWO ALTERNATIVE ROUTES, AND THE SECOND IS EXTRAORDINARILY PERMISSIVE BY UNIBZ STANDARDS. Admission-information PDF, verbatim preamble: 'In order to gain admission to this programme you need to possess an adequate knowledge of the basic disciplines of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology and fundamental knowledge of the subjects preparatory to the fundamental disciplines of this degree class. What is more, you need to hold one of the following qualifications:'

ROUTE 1 — a bachelor degree in one of four Italian degree classes: 'L-25 ex D.M. 270/2004 (Agriculture and Forestry) or the corresponding class ex D.M. 509/99; L-26 (Food Sciences) or the corresponding class ex D.M. 509/99; L-38 (Animal Production Sciences and Technologies) or the corresponding class ex D.M. 509/99; L-GASTR (Sciences, cultures and policies of Gastronomy)'. Note the inclusion of L-GASTR, the new gastronomy class created in 2021 — unibz's own Bachelor in Food and Enogastronomy Sciences feeds directly into this master.

ROUTE 2 — the route almost every foreign applicant is assessed against: 'Or the previous career must have covered at least 30 ECTS credits in one or more of the following scientific sectors'. Only THIRTY credits, and they may come from a SINGLE sector. Compare EMMA (20 + 30 = 50 ECTS across two separately-defined blocks with a two-subject-area diversity condition) or the Master in Energy Engineering (85 ECTS across three blocks). This is the loosest curricular threshold of any unibz science master examined.

THE QUALIFYING SECTOR LIST IS ALSO EXCEPTIONALLY WIDE, spanning mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, medicine, agriculture, veterinary science, mechanical/chemical/bio engineering, electronics, information processing, commodity science and statistics: MAT/01-09 (Mathematical Logic; Algebra; Geometry; Mathematics Education and History of Mathematics; Mathematical Analysis, Probability and Statistics; Mathematical Physics; Numerical Analysis; Operations Research); FIS/01-08 (Experimental Physics; Theoretical Physics and Mathematical Models and Methods; Physics of Matter; Nuclear and Subnuclear Physics; Astronomy and Astrophysics; Physics of the Earth and of the Circumterrestrial Medium; Applied Physics; Didactics and History of Physics); CHIM/01-07 (Analytical Chemistry; Physical Chemistry; General and Inorganic Chemistry; Industrial Chemistry Science and Technology of Polymeric Materials; Organic Chemistry; Chemical Foundations of Technology); CHIM/10-11 (Food Chemistry; Chemistry and Biotechnology of Fermentations); BIO/01-05 (General Botany; Systematic Botany; Environmental and Applied Botany; Plant Physiology; Zoology); BIO/09-11 (Physiology; Biochemistry; Molecular Biology); BIO/13 (Experimental Biology); BIO/18-19 (Genetics; General Microbiology); MED/07 (Microbiology and Clinical Microbiology); MED/42 (Hygiene and Public Health); AGR/01-04 (Agricultural Economics and Rural Appraisal; Agronomy and Field Crops; Arboriculture and Fruitculture; Vegetable and Ornamental Crops); AGR/07 (Agricultural Genetics); AGR/09 (Agricultural Machinery and Mechanization); AGR/11-13 (General and Applied Entomology; Plant Pathology; Agricultural Chemistry); AGR/15-19 (Food Science and Technology; Agricultural Microbiology; Livestock Systems Animal Breeding and Genetics; Animal Nutrition and Feeding; Animal Science); VET/04 (Inspection of Foods of Animal Origin); VET/06-07 (Parasitology and Animal Parasitic Diseases; Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology); ING-IND/10 (Thermal Engineering and Industrial Energy Systems); ING-IND/13-17 (Applied Mechanics; Mechanical Design and Machine Construction; Design Methods for Industrial Engineering; Manufacturing Technology and Systems; Industrial Mechanical Plants); ING-IND/23 (Applied Physical Chemistry); ING-IND/25 (Chemical Plants); ING-IND/34 (Industrial Bioengineering); ING-INF/01 (Electronics); ING-INF/05 (Information Processing Systems); SECS-P/13 (Commodity Sciences); SECS-S/01/02 (Statistics; Statistics for Experimental and Technological Research).

SSD CODE REFORM — AN IMPORTANT INCONSISTENCY INSIDE UNIBZ'S OWN DOCUMENTS. The entry-requirement list above uses only the OLD pre-2024 sector codes (MAT/, FIS/, CHIM/, BIO/, MED/, AGR/, VET/, ING-IND/, ING-INF/, SECS-). The same university's 2026/27 course catalogue for this very programme labels its teaching units exclusively with the NEW post-reform codes — AGRI-07/A (Food Science and Technology), AGRI-08/A (Agricultural Microbiology), AGRI-06/B, AGRI-04/B, AGRI-05/A, AGRI-03/A, AGRI-01/A, BIOS-06/A, MEDS-08/C, CHEM-02/A, CHEM-03/A, CHEM-05/A, CHEM-07/B. unibz has not published a mapping between the two in the admission material, so an applicant reading an Italian transcript issued after the 2024 reform must translate the new codes back to the old ones themselves. For the main equivalences relevant here: AGR/15 → AGRI-07/A, AGR/16 → AGRI-08/A, AGR/13 → AGRI-06/B, AGR/09 → AGRI-04/B, AGR/11 → AGRI-05/A, BIO/09 → BIOS-06/A, CHIM/01 → CHEM-02/A, CHIM/10 → CHEM-05/A.

FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS, verbatim from the signed ranking list: 'If you have graduated abroad, the correspondence of credit points awarded to scientific sectors will be based on the contents of the exams passed during your previous study career.' And from the admission PDF: 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' Syllabi and course descriptions should therefore be prepared in advance.

NOT YET GRADUATED: 'Applicants who do not yet have the required three-year degree may apply, but they must have the qualification by the enrolment deadline at the latest. Otherwise, they will be excluded from the procedure.' No minimum-credits-so-far condition is imposed (no '≥120 ECTS' rule as in some unibz masters).

AT ENROLMENT the Diploma Supplement must state 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. DOUBLE-ENROLMENT: at most two simultaneous programmes, not in the same class, differing in at least two-thirds of content.

READING FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: a Gıda Mühendisliği (food engineering) graduate clears the 30-ECTS threshold several times over on AGR/15-19 and CHIM/10-11 content alone. Ziraat Mühendisliği, Kimya, Kimya Mühendisliği, Biyoloji, Moleküler Biyoloji ve Genetik, Beslenme ve Diyetetik, Veteriner, Su Ürünleri and even Makine Mühendisliği or Endüstri Mühendisliği backgrounds have plausible routes through the mathematics, physics, chemistry or ING-IND sectors. Because the list includes MAT and FIS, almost any Turkish engineering or natural-science degree will contain 30 qualifying credits. The academic threshold is NOT where a Turkish applicant will fail; the non-EU quota is.

[uncertain] Unlike EMMA, this programme's documents do NOT publish a Faculty e-mail address specifically for credit-eligibility questions, and no remedial single-subject route is mentioned in the admission text. The Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it, +39 0471 017000) is the appropriate contact, and unibz's general single-subject-courses route remains available for closing a credit gap, but neither is signposted in this programme's material.
language_requirements:
ONE REQUIREMENT ONLY: ENGLISH AT B2 (CEFR) FOR ADMISSION. Verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.'

There is NO German requirement, NO Italian requirement, NO third-language B1 threshold and NO graduation/exit language requirement. This is an English-taught, not a trilingual, programme, and the 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page' line at the end of the language section is boilerplate that applies to unibz generally, not to this degree.

THE LANGUAGE GATE IS A HARD KNOCK-OUT AND IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST CAUSE OF FAILURE IN THIS APPLICATION. Failure to prove B2 means exclusion from the admission procedure regardless of grade. In the 2026/27 Early Bird EU round, EIGHT applicants (IDs 152607, 155926, 153571, 155924, 152016, 148589, 154853, 147169) were listed under 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements for admission and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure. They may re-apply in the second session.' Against 25 admitted that is roughly a quarter of the EU applicant pool — and it happened in a round that did not fill its 35 places, so those candidates lost places that were sitting empty. By comparison, the sister programme EMMA lost only 2 applicants on language in the same cycle. Whatever the cause — late uploads, missing medium-of-instruction letters, certificates older than five years, or 'home edition' online exams — this is the failure mode to plan against.

B2 IS THE FLOOR, C1 IS THE SMART TARGET: a C1-or-better certificate adds 3 points to the ranking score. For a non-EU applicant facing an 87.08/95 cut-off, three points is a meaningful number of rank positions.

WHERE TO PROVE IT: in the Application Portal, sections 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', which become available only AFTER creating an application under 'create/manage applications'.

ADMINISTRATIVE FORM: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.'

DEADLINE MECHANICS: certificates that cannot be uploaded 'can be sent by e-mail as PDF files or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline'. The Language Centre can be reached at language.centre@unibz.it, +39 0471 012400.
application_deadline_eu:
THREE POTENTIAL WINDOWS FOR EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS GIVEN PARITY OF TREATMENT, two of them fixed and published, the third discretionary. All dates below are from the 2026/27 admission-information PDF (unibz writes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO equivalents given in brackets) and all deadlines fall at NOON local time — 12:00 Central European Time, not midnight.

1. EARLY BIRD APPLICATION — 'Application: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 (by noon local time)'. ISO: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, 12:00 CET/CEST. This is the only window open to BOTH EU and non-EU applicants. It carried 35 of the 40 EU places.

2. LATE APPLICATION (ONLY FOR EU CITIZENS) — 'Application: 28/05 - 20/08/2026 (by noon local time)'. ISO: 2026-05-28 to 2026-08-20, 12:00 CEST. It carried 5 EU places, plus any Early Bird places left unfilled: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' Because the 2026/27 Early Bird EU list admitted only 25 against 35 places, roughly 15 EU places were available in the Late round — an unusually favourable position for a late EU applicant.

3. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (ONLY FOR EU CITIZENS) — 'The Faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places. More information on additional sessions will be published in due course.' No additional session for this programme had been published as of 2026-08-29.

A SECOND CHANCE AFTER FAILURE IS EXPLICITLY GRANTED: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one.' The ranking list repeats this for the language-excluded applicants: 'They may re-apply in the second session.'

STATUS ON 2026-08-29: all published EU windows for 2026/27 have closed. The Late window expired on 2026-08-20 and its ranking list was still pending, due 'by 03/09/2026'. A prospective applicant reading this is targeting 2027/28. HISTORICAL STABILITY OF THE CALENDAR, useful for planning ahead: in 2021/22 the windows were 1 March – 28 April (Early Bird) and 19 May – 24 August (Late); in 2025/26 the Late deadline was 21 August. The pattern is extremely consistent — Early Bird opens in the first days of March and closes in the last days of April; the Late window runs from late May to the third week of August. A 2027/28 applicant should plan for roughly 01/03/2027–28/04/2027 and late May to late August 2027, and confirm against the programme page from January 2027. [uncertain] The 2027/28 dates are not published; the ranges above are extrapolated from four observed cycles.
application_deadline_non_eu:
ONE SINGLE WINDOW, AND IT IS THE EARLY BIRD WINDOW: 02/03/2026 – 28/04/2026, by noon local time (ISO: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, 12:00 CET/CEST). Verbatim from the admission-information PDF: 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy) — Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.'

THIS IS THE HARDEST DEADLINE IN THE WHOLE RECORD AND THE MOST COMMON WAY A TURKISH APPLICANT LOSES A YEAR. There is no Late Application and no Additional Session for non-EU citizens living abroad — both are labelled 'only for EU citizens'. Missing 28 April means waiting a full twelve months. The 8 non-EU places are allocated entirely within this one round.

THE ASSOCIATED CALENDAR FOR A NON-EU APPLICANT IN 2026/27 WAS:
— Application 02/03–28/04/2026, noon.
— Language exams, if needed: 16/03/2026 (register 02–09/03) or 16–17 and 20–21/04/2026 (register 24/03–08/04). Note that the second sitting ends only one week before the application deadline, leaving almost no margin.
— Ranking list published by 27/05/2026.
— First instalment (EUR 600) to secure the place by 05/06/2026, noon.
— Waiting-list candidates contacted from 08/06/2026.
— Universitaly pre-enrolment and visa application: after paying the first instalment.
— Enrolment 10/07–13/10/2026, noon.

CRITICAL SEQUENCING POINT: 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal.' The visa process cannot begin until the place is paid for, which leaves roughly four months between 05/06 and 13/10 to obtain a study visa from an Italian consulate — tight but workable, provided the consulate appointment is sought immediately.

WHO COUNTS AS NON-EU LIVING ABROAD — AND THE TRAP: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The ranking list repeats it: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy... you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.' Given that the non-EU list in 2026/27 required 87.08/95 while the EU list required only 60.04, being misclassified through a missing upload is catastrophic. See parity_of_treatment.

[uncertain] The 2027/28 non-EU window is not published. On four observed cycles it has always coincided exactly with the Early Bird window opening in early March and closing in late April.
required_documents:
AT APPLICATION — four items, exactly as enumerated in the admission-information PDF:

0. VALID ID, at account creation: 'You need to create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport (front/back). Please note: if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure.'
1. QUALIFICATION: 'if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or self-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded with the final grade and passed exams (if graduated) or, if not graduated yet, a certificate listing the exams passed; if graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with the passed exams (if graduated) or transcript of records (if not graduated yet) in Italian, German or English.' Mandatory contents: 'final grade, passed exams with indication of grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles). For qualifications obtained abroad, also: scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable).'
2. EXCEL FILE: 'Please use the file available in the application portal.' The structured study-career template mapping exams onto the qualifying scientific sectors — the instrument by which the 30-ECTS threshold is verified.
3. ENGLISH LANGUAGE CERTIFICATIONS 'at least of level B2', or medium-of-instruction evidence, or registration for a unibz Language Centre exam.
PLUS, for foreign qualifications: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.'
PLUS, for parity-of-treatment applicants: a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno, or the renewal request if expired.

AT ENROLMENT, for holders of a foreign university degree — three base items plus a country-dependent recognition package:
— 'degree diploma of your Bachelor';
— 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)';
— 'Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'.
Then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein — ARDI Statement of Correspondence; (b) non-EU Lisbon Convention signatories — ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND CIMEA Statement of Verification; (c) non-EU non-signatories — CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND CIMEA Statement of Verification. See credential_recognition.
For non-EU citizens living abroad, additionally: the entry visa for study/university and, after arrival, the residence permit handed in to the Student Office.

DOCUMENTS AN APPLICANT MIGHT EXPECT BUT DOES NOT NEED: no CV, no motivation letter, no reference letters, no research or thesis proposal, no portfolio, no video, no GRE/GMAT report, no proof of funds at application stage (that belongs to the visa process), no health certificate.

STRONGLY ADVISABLE THOUGH NOT LISTED: course syllabi and content descriptions, because 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary'; and, for any applicant claiming a national academic distinction, documentary evidence of it, since the cum laude mapping is undefined.

CHECKLIST FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT, in the order the items take longest to obtain: (1) the registrar's medium-of-instruction letter — free, fast, and worth +3 points; (2) the official English transcript WITH the printed grading-scale legend showing 4.00 maximum and 2.00 minimum — this is the item most often missing and it is load-bearing for the entire score; (3) the diploma and Diploma Supplement showing ≥180 ECTS and access to master studies; (4) CIMEA Statement of Comparability and Statement of Verification — Turkey is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so the ARDI route plus CIMEA verification applies, and CIMEA processing takes weeks, so start immediately after admission; (5) the completed portal Excel file.

HARD RULES: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' 'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents.' 'Please note that if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'
entry_exam_or_test:
NO ENTRANCE EXAM OF ANY KIND. Specifically absent: no unibz admission test; no TOLC (TOLC-I, TOLC-E, TOLC-S or TOLC-B); no CENT-S; no SAT, GRE or GMAT and no GMAT/GRE bonus; no subject test; no oral interview; no portfolio review; no video presentation; no laboratory practical. Admission is decided purely on uploaded documents plus an arithmetic score computed from the bachelor grade.

THE ONLY EXAM AN APPLICANT MIGHT SIT is the ENGLISH LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY EXAM run by the unibz Language Centre, and only if they cannot prove B2 English through the medium of instruction of their high school or degree, or through a recognised certificate. It is held ONLINE and is computer-based. 2026/27 sittings and their registration windows, verbatim from the admission-information PDF:
— Early Bird: '16/03/2026 (registration: 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration: 24/03 - 08/04/2026)';
— Late: '22 - 26/06/2026 (registration: 28/05 - 15/06/2026) and 27/07 (registration: 10 - 19/07/2026)'.

PROCEDURAL TRAP, verbatim: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' Registration is done in the Application Portal under 'enrol for language exams', which only becomes available after an application has been created under 'create/manage applications'. Given that eight EU applicants were excluded on language grounds in Early Bird 2026/27, this is the operationally riskiest step in the whole application.

NOTE ON WHAT THE LANGUAGE EXAM CANNOT DO FOR YOU: the unibz internal exam is recognised at B1, B2 and C1 levels, so a candidate who sits it and achieves C1 also earns the +3 ranking bonus. A candidate who achieves only B2 is admitted to the procedure but scores nothing extra.
tuition_or_fees_link:
EUR 1,200 PER YEAR, in two instalments. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'Fees amount to € 1200. 1st instalment (€ 600): includes the revenue stamp of € 16. 2nd instalment (€ 600): must be paid by March of the following year. Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied. If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes. If you drop out of a programme, interrupt your studies or are excluded from studies, you are not entitled to reimbursement of the fees.' The brochure 'At a Glance' box states 'Tuition fees: ca. € 1200 per year'. Over the two-year degree the total is therefore approximately EUR 2,400.

THE FIRST INSTALMENT DOUBLES AS THE PLACE-SECURING PAYMENT. For 2026/27 Early Bird it had to be paid by 05/06/2026 at noon, and for the Late round by 11/09/2026 at noon. Missing it forfeits the place to the next person on the ranking list.

EXEMPTIONS, verbatim: 'Exemption from the tuition fees is granted to: Students with a disability recognized under article 3, paragraph 1, of Law No 104/1992, or with a disability up to or exceeding 66%: the disability certificate, issued by the health authorities, must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year. Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government.' And: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.'

REFUND POSITION: 'Paying university fees does not confer student status, which is only obtained by enrolling. If you pay but do not enrol, you are not entitled to a refund, except for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country.' This last exception is the safety net for a Turkish applicant who pays, then fails to obtain a visa.

CONTEXT — THIS IS CHEAP AND HAS GOT CHEAPER. EUR 1,200 is a flat fee unrelated to income, nationality or ISEE, which is unusual in the Italian system and strongly favourable to international students, who at most Italian state universities pay income-assessed fees that can be far higher without an ISEE-parificato. It is also lower than it used to be: AlmaLaurea records an annual cost of EUR 1,350 for the 2024/25 cohort and EUR 1,200 for 2025/26, and the 2019/20-era figure for the sister programme EMMA was EUR 1,347.50.

uncertainty_notes:
DATA VINTAGE. Everything in this record describes the 2026/27 cycle, from unibz documents footed 'Latest update: 24.07.2026' and from the signed 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list, all retrieved on 2026-08-29. On that date the 2026/27 cycle was effectively closed: both EU windows and the single non-EU window had expired, and only enrolment formalities remained. A reader planning an application is planning for 2027/28, for which NO dates, quotas or fees have been published. The observed calendar has been stable across four cycles (Early Bird opening in the first days of March and closing in the last days of April; Late running from late May to the third week of August), so those ranges are a reasonable planning basis, but they are extrapolations.

THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT UNRESOLVED QUESTION — WHERE THE SECOND YEAR PHYSICALLY HAPPENS. unibz's brochure lists 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano' with no second campus, and the 2026/27 unibz course catalogue lists the Udine and Parma profile courses INSIDE the unibz offering, taught by Udine and Parma professors, all tagged EN. The University of Parma, by contrast, describes profile-specific teaching as taking place at the partner universities in the third semester, and unibz's own programme page says students 'will have the opportunity to spend up to two semesters in one of these European partner institutions'. These two pictures are not reconcilable from public sources. The difference matters for housing, cost of living, residence-permit address updates and — for the University College Cork path — a possible move to a different country's immigration system. This must be settled with the Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it, +39 0471 017000) before a candidate commits.

THE JOINT-DEGREE MECHANICS ARE UNDOCUMENTED. That the award is a joint degree ('rilascio del titolo congiunto') is stated plainly by Udine and by Parma and is not in doubt. But the underlying inter-university convention is not published by any of the three universities, and nothing public explains how the diploma is issued, whether the partner universities levy any fee, how the 5 University College Cork places are allocated, or whether profile choice is free or competitive.

TEMPLATE ERRORS IN UNIBZ'S OWN DOCUMENTS, recorded so they are not mistaken for data: the admission-information PDF's double-enrolment example says 'LM-73 and LM-73' (EMMA's class), and the ranking list's second statement of the same rule says 'LM-18/LM-18' (Software Engineering's class). The correct class is LM-70, confirmed by the brochure, the programme page, the University of Udine and AlmaLaurea, and used correctly in the ranking list's first statement of the rule.

NAMING INCONSISTENCY: the brochure calls the Udine profile 'Food Quality and Management' on page 3 and 'Food Quality Control and Management' on page 4. The latter matches the 2021 Parma documentation.

THE SCORING CONVERSION IS DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED. The model base = 5 × (grade out of 30) − 55, capped at 95, with +2 cum laude and +3 for C1, fits the published minimum (55 = 22/30), the maximum (95 = 30/30) and the sister programme EMMA's integer distribution, and it is the only model tested that does not produce impossible sub-18/30 grades for the lowest waiting-list scores. It should nonetheless be treated as a strong working model rather than an official rule.

AN UNEXPLAINED ANOMALY IN THE RANKING LIST: the stated minimum is 55/95, yet non-EU waiting-list ranks 37 and 38 carry scores of 53.73 and 51.45. Unlike EMMA's list, this one has no 'below the minimum score' exclusion section, so it cannot be determined whether the minimum is applied only at the moment of admission or whether the waiting list is simply published in full. Practical effect is limited — nobody near the bottom of a 30-person waiting list was ever going to be admitted — but the rule's exact operation is unclear.

CONFLICTING SECONDARY DATA. AlmaLaurea records the admission committee as awarding 'up to 100 points' for both 2024/25 and 2025/26, while unibz's own current documents say 95; AlmaLaurea also gives EUR 1,350 as the 2024/25 annual cost against EUR 1,200 now. Where AlmaLaurea and unibz disagree, the unibz document governs. AlmaLaurea's 'five distinct profiles' phrasing is likewise stale — there are four.

SOURCES THAT COULD NOT BE READ. The University of Parma's live course page (corsi.unipr.it) serves a JavaScript CAPTCHA human-verification wall to automated clients and was not accessed; the Parma information in this record therefore comes from the University of Udine's parallel page, from Parma's own 2021/22 PDF brochure on its albo pretorio, and from search-engine extracts of the Parma page. The unibz grade-statistics page for this programme returns HTTP 200 but loads its figures dynamically and yielded no static content, so no exam-grade or final-grade distribution could be captured — a gap relative to the EMMA record, which has one.

FIGURES TAKEN FROM SECONDARY SUMMARIES RATHER THAN PRIMARY PAGES: the provincial study-grant range of EUR 1,680–6,960, the 27/30 merit threshold, the two-year residence rule for non-EU merit applicants, and the part-time fee halving. All are consistent with unibz's Study Guide as summarised, but the primary Study Guide pages redirected in ways that prevented direct capture during this pass, and provincial amounts are re-set annually.

NOT DOCUMENTED ANYWHERE: how a non-Italian 'with honours' distinction maps onto the +2 cum laude bonus; whether a non-Italian graduate can sit the Tecnologo Alimentare state examination; health-insurance requirements for the study visa; the amount of the late-payment fine on the second instalment; and the founding year, which is taken from AlmaLaurea's 'inception 2018' record rather than from a unibz announcement.

STILL PENDING AT THE VERIFICATION DATE: the 2026/27 Late Application ranking list, due by 03/09/2026, which will show whether the EU side finally filled; and any Additional Application Session, which the Faculty may open for EU citizens given that the EU Early Bird list admitted only 25 against 35 places.
